Taan rides third class; if need be, hiding behind her two-month-old copy of the London Times. Long after sunset, less than an hour from Nairobi, she judges that the time is right. From the safety of the third-class car toilet she summons and binds two fire vampires; one burns with a blue flame, the other red. Assuming Taan Kaur has been notified to expect their arrival, she takes the same train as the investigators. Taan rides third class; if need be, hiding behind her two-month-old copy of the London Times. Long after sunset, less than an hour from Nairobi, she judges that the time is right. From the safety of the third-class car toilet she summons and binds two fire vampires; one burns with a blue flame, the other red. Like living stars, the entities hover in the night just outside the window, then drift down the length of the train; occasional screams and shouts of astonishment mark the progress of these swirling, flaming apparitions. Beside their targets, the walls of the coach begin to buckle, discolor, and smoke as the merciless things burn their way in: bound to Taan Kaur, they attack until the investigators die, Taan is killed or rendered unconscious, or until they themselves are destroyed.

PULP: BURNING RAILS

This scene can become far more over the top in a pulp setting. Surely no pulp-style train journey is complete without characters standing atop the moving train carriages; in this case, battling balls of flame or perhaps dueling a Mythos sorcerer. In desperation, Taan might escape by leaping from the train, only to appear later in the game.

Taan Kaur summons the red and blue fire vampires from the third-class toilet and binds them to her. They continue attacking until the investigators die, Taan is killed or knocked unconscious, or the vampires themselves are destroyed.

The red and blue fire vampires are summoned and bound by Taan Kaur from the third-class toilet. They attack until the investigators die, Taan dies or loses consciousness, or the vampires are destroyed. Ordinary material weapons, including bullets and blades, do no harm. Pouring half a gallon of water on a fire vampire removes one hit point; a bucket of water deals 1D3 damage and a typical handheld fire extinguisher deals 1D6. Toilet pitchers each hold about a gallon of water, the dining car has nearly 40 gallons (180 liters), and the locomotive tender holds hundreds of gallons that could be used if a sufficiently fast draining method is found. Bottles of alcohol are not recommended as substitutes for water, particularly whisky and brandy, which only encourage the fire vampires. Other substances may have effects, but this does not establish a universal liquid damage rule.

Taan Kaur summons and binds the two fire vampires from the third-class toilet. Their attacks end if the investigators die, Taan is killed or knocked unconscious, or the vampires themselves are destroyed. Toilet pitchers each contain about a gallon of water, the dining car has nearly 40 gallons (180 liters), and the locomotive tender has hundreds of gallons available if a fast enough draining method can be found. Bottles of alcohol are not recommended as substitutes for water, particularly whisky and brandy, which only encourage the fire vampires. Ordinary blades and bullets cannot harm the vampires, while water and fire extinguishers can hurt them.
